items.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to embarrassing farrago but issues do not stop here
items.summary:
After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance

A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history.

As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday, was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute.

items.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
items.summary:
The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups

A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early.

The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered.

items.t: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?

items.title: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame
items.summary:
The job of Mauricio Pochettino’s successor is to fine-tune a team on the up. That requires a bureaucrat rather than a figurehead

First, let’s get the Pep Exception out of the way. Or perhaps we’d better call it the Guardiola Caveat. Regardless, the point is the same. If US Soccer can get Pep Guardiola to manage the United States men’s national team, it should. Because when you have the chance to employ the most successful and influential coach of his generation, the thinker who stands upstream of essentially every major tactical current of the last two decades, you just have to do it.

But let us assume that US Soccer can’t appoint Guardiola, because he is only a few months into his post-Manchester City sabbatical and still busying himself defending his body of work. Because he has given no recent indication that he wants the job, even though he spent a previous break between managerial gigs living in New York City and was probably only being supportive of his newly-appointed colleague Mauricio Pochettino when he called the project “fascinating” two years ago. Also because he has only ever signed on to coach teams stacked with Ballon d’Or contenders, posing a Phil Jackson-type, bar-room question over whether he would still be exceptional in charge of unexceptional players.

items.t: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame

items.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
items.summary:
A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979

Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio.

Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer.

items.t: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals

items.title: ‘It’s stressful but better than having a proper job’: the life of a cricket umpire
items.summary:
Four umpires discuss how they deal with players, why they avoid social media, how technology is changing cricket and why umpiring beats being a football referee

By Wisden Cricket Monthly

Last summer, sat in a quiet ground at the fag-end of a four-dayer, with a few souls still kicking around and a clutch of cameras streaming what was left of the day live on YouTube, it struck me again what a great, strange sanctuary this place is, out there on the edges of the modern world. The game is trying to move, albeit at its own pace. Later that night, the day’s highlights would be landing on social media, available to all, for the game’s devotees to pore over and pick apart.

More people are watching the County Championship than ever before. Streaming numbers show a growing audience in the UK and a widening uptake across the cricketing globe. The numbers aren’t yet earth-shattering, but how could they be, with such eccentric fare?

“Ronaldinho played for Ravenna, in Serie C, earlier this month. It was his first professional appearance in more than 11 years,” writes George Jones. “Have any other footballers had long career hiatuses? And has any player had a longer hiatus than 11 years?”

Ronaldinho’s last professional appearance before his return for Ravenna came on 26 September 2015 for Fluminense, who won 2-0 at home against Goiás. He was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Fans of symmetry will be pleased to see that 11 years and 50 days later, the Brazilian returned for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against another team with five letters and an accent in their name, Forlì, and was withdrawn after 45 minutes.

items.title: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov
items.summary:
• Opening game ends in draw by repetition

  • Defending champion plays white in Game 2

  • Read our move-by-move report of Game 1

  • Sindarov: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

Indian chess star Gukesh Dommaraju held off Javokhir Sindarov amid a mounting time crisis on Tuesday, drawing the opening game of their eagerly awaited $2.5m world title match in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the picturesque Geneva suburb of Cologny.

After spending more than 36 minutes on a single move and much of the afternoon racing against the clock, the defending champion said the time he invested early helped him play faster as a drawish position sharpened and his minutes dwindled opposite the in-form Uzbek challenger. “When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves,” Gukesh said. “And then the moves after that were pretty easy.”

items.title: The Breakdown | North v south: who makes the cut in our fantasy XVs for a hemisphere head-to-head?
items.summary:
Before the Nations Championship finale, picking MVPs for all-star hemisphere teams plus a global XV is far from easy

This week the world’s top 400 rugby players will be assembling in the same city. You can only hope London’s steak restaurants and cafes are braced for the simultaneous influx of an army of huge men with even larger appetites. If tall buildings start to sway in the Twickenham area, you will know the buildup to this weekend’s Nations Championship finals is intensifying.

Which begs a timely question. Mirror, mirror on the wall, who’s the most valuable of them all? With this week billed as a north v south duel – there is even a trophy on offer to the champion hemisphere – it is not a bad moment to sit down with pen and paper and play fantasy selector. Name two all-star XVs to represent north and south respectively. And which of them would win if they went head to head?

items.title: Philippe Diallo learns harsh reality of mounting global challenge to Infantino
items.summary:
French Football Federation president faces uphill battle to win backing of Africa’s decision-makers in Fifa election

Philippe Diallo must be learning very quickly that the battle to wrest the Fifa presidency from Gianni Infantino will be very challenging.

When Patrice Motsepe, the president of the Confederation of African Football (Caf), asked the presidents and general secretaries of its 54 member associations to give Infantino a standing ovation at Caf’s general assembly last weekend, Diallo, a guest at the event, had no choice but to cope with an uncomfortable moment.

items.title: Game over? How playing Grand Theft Auto VI is affecting elite athletes’ performances | Sean Ingle
items.summary:
Burning the midnight oil playing video games is not ideal preparation for professional sport – but it’s not all bad

“They miss games, the cheque’s still clearing. And you’re trying to tell me they got this kind of addiction to a video game that they sitting there with their thumbs looking like Donald Trump?” That was ESPN’s Stephen A Smith, one of the US’s most provocative and influential sports pundits, spitting fire and fury last week after hearing that so many NBA and NFL stars were absorbed in Grand Theft Auto VI.

Smith was hardly an outlier. Other pundits, as well as some Manchester United fans, also questioned Bryan Mbeumo’s focus and professionalism after he posted an image of GTA VI and the word “historique” after midnight on Thursday. Meanwhile before last weekend’s Premier League games, the Odd Sport social media account predicted that Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City would all lose. Why? Because their younger squads might be more focused on Vice City than their opponents, and therefore play with less intensity as a result. By Monday that forecast had been liked tens of thousands of times.
